intro: Read a short fictional news report and distinguish its main facts from the headline.
b1.texto: In a short news item, use the first sentence and the time or place expressions to locate the event. Then check the details: who is affected, when a change begins and whether the text gives a reason. This report is fictional and is used only for language practice.
b2.f0: The library in the San Miguel neighbourhood will extend its opening hours from next Monday.
b2.f1: From Monday to Thursday it will close at eight in the evening, two hours later than it does now.
b2.f2: The town council says the change responds to requests from students and workers.
b2.f3: On Saturdays, the opening hours will stay the same.
b2.f4: The reading room will open at nine and offer internet access throughout the extended opening hours.
b2.f5: The report does not specify whether more staff will be in the building during those hours.
b4.pregunta: When will the new opening hours begin?
b4.o1.refuerzo: Check the information in the text or rule.
b4.o2.refuerzo: This option does not fit the context.
b5.pregunta: How much later will the library close from Monday to Thursday?
b5.o1.refuerzo: Check the information in the text or rule.
b5.o2.refuerzo: This option does not fit the context.
b6.o1.refuerzo: Check the information in the text or rule.
b6.o2.refuerzo: This option does not fit the context.
b7.o2.refuerzo: This form does not fit the sentence.
b8.o0: The town council says the change responds to the requests.
b8.o1: The residents explain that the library is closed.
b8.o1.explicacion: Check the meaning of the Spanish sentence.
b8.o2: The town council says the change has been cancelled.
b8.o2.explicacion: Check the meaning of the Spanish sentence.
b9.traduccion: The library will extend its opening hours on Monday.
